title: Ionic Small Examples
description: Use these small Ionic examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Build a page shell
examples.description: IonPage groups a screen, and IonContent gives it a scrolling content area.
examples.code:
import {IonApp,IonPage,IonHeader,IonToolbar,IonTitle,IonContent} from "@ionic/react"; export default function App(){return Reading club

Choose a story today.

;}
examples.output: The starter app displays a Reading club header and a padded content area.

examples.title: Use a styled button
examples.description: IonButton is a button component with Ionic styles.
examples.output: Each click increases the displayed count.

examples.title: Group rows in a list
examples.description: IonList groups list rows. IonItem supplies row layout, and IonLabel holds its text.
examples.code:
import {IonApp,IonPage,IonHeader,IonToolbar,IonTitle,IonContent,IonList,IonItem,IonLabel} from "@ionic/react";
export default function App(){return <IonApp><IonPage><IonHeader><IonToolbar><IonTitle>Reading club</IonTitle></IonToolbar></IonHeader><IonContent className="ion-padding"><IonList><IonItem><IonLabel>Moon Trip</IonLabel></IonItem><IonItem><IonLabel>Garden Days</IonLabel></IonItem></IonList></IonContent></IonPage></IonApp>;}
examples.output: Two book rows appear inside the list.

examples.title: Show a card
examples.description: An Ionic card groups a title and related content.
examples.code:
import {IonApp,IonPage,IonHeader,IonToolbar,IonTitle,IonContent,IonCard,IonCardHeader,IonCardTitle,IonCardContent} from "@ionic/react";
export default function App(){return <IonApp><IonPage><IonHeader><IonToolbar><IonTitle>Reading club</IonTitle></IonToolbar></IonHeader><IonContent className="ion-padding"><IonCard><IonCardHeader><IonCardTitle>Book of the week</IonCardTitle></IonCardHeader><IonCardContent>A story about a moon garden.</IonCardContent></IonCard></IonContent></IonPage></IonApp>;}
examples.output: The page shows one styled card with a heading and description.

examples.title: Read a labelled input
examples.description: IonInput can manage a typed value with React state.
examples.output: The greeting follows the typed name.

examples.title: Choose an option
examples.description: IonSelect offers a controlled list of choices.
examples.output: The current book type changes after a selection.

examples.title: Use a checkbox
examples.output: Checking the box changes the message to Ready.

examples.title: Create responsive columns
examples.description: Ionic's grid uses rows and columns. A column can use a different share of the row at a wider breakpoint.
examples.code:
import {IonApp,IonPage,IonHeader,IonToolbar,IonTitle,IonContent,IonGrid,IonRow,IonCol} from "@ionic/react";
export default function App(){return <IonApp><IonPage><IonHeader><IonToolbar><IonTitle>Reading club</IonTitle></IonToolbar></IonHeader><IonContent className="ion-padding"><IonGrid><IonRow><IonCol size="12" sizeMd="6">Stories</IonCol><IonCol size="12" sizeMd="6">Science</IonCol></IonRow></IonGrid></IonContent></IonPage></IonApp>;}
examples.output: The columns stack on narrow screens and share a row from the md breakpoint.

examples.title: Show a short toast message
examples.description: A toast is a short status message that appears briefly.
examples.output: The button opens a two-second message, then the dismiss event resets the state.

examples.title: Open and close a modal
examples.description: A modal is a focused layer above a page.
examples.output: The help button opens a modal, and the close button dismisses it.

examples.title: Show loading as its own state
examples.description: Loading, empty and failed are different states.
examples.code:
import {IonApp,IonPage,IonHeader,IonToolbar,IonTitle,IonContent,IonSpinner} from "@ionic/react"; export default function App(){return Reading club

Loading the book list...

;}
examples.output: The app shows a spinner and a readable loading message.

examples.title: Build the browser app first
examples.description: Ionic uses web code. A browser build can be tested before optional native packaging with tools such as Capacitor.
examples.code:
Run the starter's build command.
Preview its production web output.
Test keyboard use and small-screen layout.
Check local state after a reload.
Add native packaging only when the project needs device features.
examples.output: You get a tested web version before adding platform packaging complexity.
